advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Broaden the signing guard in record_completion_verdict (or the sign_completion_verdict contract) so a non-SigningError cannot violate the documented 'NEVER raises' recorder guarantee.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:241 `try:` then `sign_completion_verdict(result, resolved_id, repo_root)` guarded only by `except _signing.SigningError as exc:`

Docstring at transition_close.py: 'Best-effort and NEVER raises: recording is observability plus a close-time optimization, so a sidecar or signing failure leaves the caller's verdict/exit untouched.'
The sidecar emit above it defensively catches broad `except Exception:` (transition_close.py:220), so the two halves are asymmetric in their guarantee.
advisory.finding: record_completion_verdict documents a strict 'Best-effort and NEVER raises' contract, but the signing block catches only _signing.SigningError. If sign_completion_verdict's _verdict_manifest or signing.sign_manifest raises any other exception (e.g. OSError/ValueError on a malformed manifest or store fault), it propagates out of record_completion_verdict and — since the CLI/MCP call it after the verdict is computed — would turn a completed verify into a hard error, contradicting the documented never-raises guarantee.

advisory.finding: The new --no-sign CLI flag (added to the verify-completion parser and wired as `sign=not args.no_sign`) has no test driving it end-to-end. No test invokes `main(["verify-completion", tid, "--no-sign"])` on an attested PASS and asserts that no completion-verifier attestation is signed (only the sidecar is written). The library-level test covers sign=False directly but never proves the CLI flag maps to it, so a regression that ignores or inverts the flag goes undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_verify_completion_facades.py, add a test that monkeypatches verify_completion to return an attested PASS, runs `main(["verify-completion", tid, "--no-sign"])`, and asserts verify_signature verdict != 'certified' while the sidecar is present.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests for the `no_verified_sha` cause (attested PASS without verified_at_sha) and the `sign_failed` cause (monkeypatch sign_completion_verdict to raise SigningError, assert outcome cause=='sign_failed' and no exception propagates).

advisory.finding: Two documented `cause` branches of record_completion_verdict are unexercised: `no_verified_sha` (attested certifiable PASS missing verified_at_sha) and `sign_failed` (sign_completion_verdict raising SigningError). The `sign_failed` path also guards the stated best-effort/never-raises contract; without a test injecting a SigningError, a regression that lets it propagate would break the caller's verdict/exit undetected.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Mirror the standalone completion recording onto the library sibling rebar.llm.verify_completion (record/sign by default) so it matches review_plan's library-layer signing, rather than recording only in the CLI and MCP adapters.
evidence: Diff adds recording to CLI: src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:265 `result["record"] = record_completion_verdict(result, args.ticket_id, sign=not args.no_sign)`
Diff adds recording to MCP: src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:178 `result["record"] = record_completion_verdict(result, ticket_id, sign=not _readonly())`

Sibling library adapter unchanged and lacks any sign/record param: src/rebar/llm/completion.py:120-130 `def verify_completion(ticket_id, *, graph=None, ref=None, source=None, fetch=True, repo_root=None, config=None, runner=None) -> dict:`

Claimed symmetry places recording in the library for review_plan: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:421 `sign: bool = True,` (both CLI _llm_commands.py:361 and MCP _mcp_llm.py:238 merely surface it), so the completion equivalent's library sibling rebar.llm.verify_completion is the divergent surface.
advisory.finding: The new standalone completion-recording surface (record_completion_verdict, sign-by-default) was added to the CLI verify-completion handler and the MCP verify_completion tool, but the sibling LIBRARY adapter rebar.llm.verify_completion (src/rebar/llm/completion.py) was NOT updated: it neither records nor exposes a sign/record parameter. The diff bases its symmetry on review_plan, whose sign surface lives in the library core (rebar.llm.review_plan(*, sign=True)); the completion equivalent placed recording only in the two thin adapters, so a caller using the library surface directly gets no recording/signing and a later same-ref close cannot reuse the verdict.
scenarios: A programmatic caller invoking rebar.llm.verify_completion(...) directly (rather than through the CLI verb or MCP tool) obtains an attested PASS but nothing is signed/recorded, so a subsequent same-ref close re-runs the (billable) completion verifier — the exact duplicate-run defect the diff sets out to fix, but only closed on two of three surfaces.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Suppress the COMPLETION_VERDICT sidecar write when the MCP server is read-only (thread an emit_sidecar/record flag through record_completion_verdict, symmetric with review_plan's emit_sidecar=not ro), or otherwise ensure verify_completion performs no store writes in readonly mode.
evidence: transition_close.py:218-226: `sidecar_written = completion_sidecar.emit(result, material=None, repo_root=repo_root)` runs unconditionally, before any of the `sign`/source/certifiable guards
transition_close.py:233 `if not sign:` only affects the signing branch — there is no parameter to suppress the sidecar emit
_mcp_llm.py:178: `result["record"] = record_completion_verdict(result, ticket_id, sign=not _readonly())` — only signing is gated on readonly
_mcp_llm.py:125: verify_completion is declared `@mcp.tool(annotations=_ANN["READ_ONLY_OPEN_WORLD"])`
_mcp_llm.py:235-239: the sibling review_plan gates the sidecar too: `ro = _readonly()` then `review_plan(..., sign=not ro, emit_sidecar=not ro, ...)`
_seam.py:534-541: append_event `commits + pushes IN-PROCESS via write_and_push` — a genuine store mutation, not observability-only in memory
blocking.finding: In MCP read-only mode, the READ_ONLY_OPEN_WORLD-annotated verify_completion tool still performs a store mutation: record_completion_verdict unconditionally emits the COMPLETION_VERDICT sidecar (a committed and pushed append_event) before the sign gate, and the sign=not _readonly() flag only suppresses the signature — not the sidecar write. The sibling review_plan suppresses both by passing emit_sidecar=not ro.
scenarios: An operator runs the MCP server in REBAR_MCP_READONLY mode and invokes verify_completion; a COMPLETION_VERDICT event is committed and pushed to the ticket store despite the read-only posture and the READ_ONLY_OPEN_WORLD annotation.
blocking.suggested_fix: Add an `emit_sidecar: bool = True` (or `record`) parameter to record_completion_verdict that gates the completion_sidecar.emit call, and have the MCP verify_completion pass `emit_sidecar=not _readonly()` (as review_plan already does), so a read-only server performs no store write.
